title: Internal-action module presheaves and the sheaf condition on the twisted site
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(C,J)$ be a $\mathcal V$-small site with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $K:C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Grp}$ be a sheaf of groups with $\mathcal V$-small values. Write $C_K$ for the category with the objects of $C$, arrows $(f,a):V\to U$ consisting of $f:V\to U$ and $a\in K(V)$, identities $(1,1)$ and composition $(f,a)\circ(g,b)=(fg,b\,g^*a)$. Equip $C_K$ with the Grothendieck topology generated by families whose underlying families are $J$-coverings [lem-sfb-twisted-site-sieve-geometry]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative unital rings on $C$, with $\mathcal V$-small values, given the trivial $K$-action. A $K$-equivariant presheaf of $R$-modules is a presheaf of $R$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] with operations $K(U)\times P(U)\to P(U)$ natural in $U$, satisfying the left group-action laws and $R(U)$-linearity in the second variable; its morphisms are restriction-natural, equivariant componentwise linear maps. An equivariant sheaf has underlying module presheaf a sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

The ring presheaf $R_K(U)=R(U)$, $R_K(f,a)=f^*$ is a sheaf on $C_K$. The formula $E(P)(U)=P(U)$, $E(P)(f,a)(m)=a\cdot f^*m$, and the same component maps on morphisms, defines an additive equivalence from $K$-equivariant presheaves of $R$-modules to presheaves of $R_K$-modules on $C_K$. Its inverse has restrictions $N(f,1)$ and action $a\cdot n=N(1_U,a)(n)$; the two constructions are inverse on objects and morphisms. Moreover $E(P)$ is a sheaf if and only if $P$ is a sheaf on $C$. Thus these functors restrict to an additive equivalence from equivariant $R$-module sheaves to $\operatorname{Mod}(R_K)$, with those same section modules, morphisms, restrictions and recovered actions.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-twisted-site-sieve-geometry] for the category and its topology. Write $J^{\mathrm{gen}}$ for the topology generated by the base coverings. Its sieve bijection says that every covering sieve on $U$ in $C_K$ is $S_T=\{(f,a)\mid f\in T\}$ for a unique $J^{\mathrm{gen}}$-covering sieve $T$ in $C$. It also gives $(f,a)=(f,1)\circ(1,a)$. These statements apply because $C$ is small with finite limits and $K$ is the given small-valued group sheaf.

source.place: Paragraph (3), categorical foundation: covering-sieve comparison used in returned step 6

proof.text: For any presheaf of sets $P$ with a natural left $K$-action define $F_P(f,a)x=a\cdot f^*x$. For composable $(f,a),(g,b)$, naturality of the action and its multiplication law give $F_P(g,b)F_P(f,a)x=b\cdot g^*(a\cdot f^*x)=(b\,g^*a)\cdot(fg)^*x=F_P(fg,b\,g^*a)x$. Also $F_P(1,1)x=x$. Thus these formulas define a presheaf; this calculation uses exactly the composition established in step 1.

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned step 4: explicit contravariant functor law

proof.text: For a base sieve $T$ on $U$, a matching family $x_f\in P(\operatorname{dom}f)$ extends to a matching family on $S_T$ by $y_{(f,a)}=a\cdot x_f$: for $(g,b)$ its restriction is $b\cdot g^*(a\cdot x_f)=(b\,g^*a)\cdot x_{fg}=y_{(fg,b\,g^*a)}$. Conversely any matching family $y$ gives $x_f=y_{(f,1)}$; matching along $(g,1)$ gives $g^*x_f=x_{fg}$, and along $(1,a)$ gives $y_{(f,a)}=a\cdot x_f$. These assignments are inverse. A section $x\in P(U)$ amalgamates $x_f$ exactly when it amalgamates $y_{(f,a)}$, since $F_P(f,a)x=a\cdot f^*x$. This proves a bijection of matching families respecting the identical set of amalgamations, by the definition in [def-weil-pbc-topos].

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned step 6: matching families, including all labels

proof.text: Work directly with the sieve sheaf conditions for the two Grothendieck topologies already appearing in the Lean statement. The order isomorphism of step 1 identifies their covering sieves, and step 3 identifies their matching families with the same amalgamations. The underlying-sets criterion for abelian groups therefore proves the asserted sheaf equivalence. No conversion from a pretopology sheaf condition is needed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned step 6: comparison with the base site sheaf condition

proof.text: For the coefficient sheaf, equip the rank-one module presheaf of the underlying ring sheaf with the trivial action. Its extended underlying set presheaf is definitionally the underlying set presheaf of R_K. Apply step 4 and the underlying-sets sheaf criteria for commutative rings and abelian groups. Thus R_K is a sheaf, without invoking the parent presentation theorem or its coefficient_isSheaf hole.

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned step 6: ring-sheaf clause, before module constructions

proof.text: For an equivariant module presheaf $P$, step 2 gives the restriction maps of $E(P)$. They are additive, and for $r\in R(U)$ and $m\in P(U)$ they satisfy $E(P)(f,a)(rm)=a\cdot(f^*r\,f^*m)=f^*r\,(a\cdot f^*m)$ by linearity of the action. Hence they are semilinear over $R_K(f,a)$, exactly as required in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. If $h:P\to Q$ is restriction-natural, equivariant and componentwise linear, then $h_V(a\cdot f^*m)=a\cdot f^*h_U(m)$. Thus the same components define $E(h)$; identity and composition are unchanged.

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned step 4: module and morphism formulas

proof.text: Conversely let $N$ be a presheaf of $R_K$-modules. Put $P(U)=N(U)$, $f^*=N(f,1)$, and $a\cdot n=N(1_U,a)n$. The label-one arrows compose as in $C$, so these restrictions form a module presheaf. Since $(1,b)\circ(1,a)=(1,ab)$, contravariance gives $N(1,ab)=N(1,a)N(1,b)$; the identity gives $1\cdot n=n$. Thus this is a left action, and it is $R(U)$-linear because $R_K(1,a)=1$. Finally $(1_U,a)\circ(f,1)=(f,f^*a)=(f,1)\circ(1_V,f^*a)$ gives $N(f,1)N(1_U,a)=N(1_V,f^*a)N(f,1)$, the required naturality. Naturality of a morphism of module presheaves at $(f,1)$ and $(1,a)$ supplies restriction-naturality and equivariance of its unchanged components.

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned step 5: recovered action and its naturality

proof.text: Starting with $P$, the recovered restrictions and action are $E(P)(f,1)=f^*$ and $E(P)(1,a)m=a\cdot m$. Starting with $N$, the reconstructed restriction is $N(1,a)N(f,1)=N((f,1)\circ(1,a))=N(f,a)$ by step 1 and contravariance. On morphisms both round trips retain each component. Thus the functors are inverse (with identity comparison maps on the section modules). Hom groups in both categories have pointwise addition: sums preserve linearity, naturality and equivariance by distributivity. Because both functors keep every component, they preserve addition and zero, proving additivity.

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned steps 4--5: inverse and additive equivalence

proof.text: For each equivariant module presheaf $P$, its underlying set presheaf satisfies step 4, so $E(P)$ is a sheaf exactly when $P$ is a sheaf. A module sheaf is precisely a module presheaf satisfying that underlying sheaf condition, with the same componentwise linear morphisms [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Therefore both inverse functors of step 8 restrict to the asserted full subcategories of sheaves, retain their component maps and additivity, and have exactly the section modules, restrictions and actions in the statement.

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned step 6: restriction of the inverse equivalence to sheaves
